title: Micron Shares Fall 12% in Five Sessions as Funds Add Shares
text:
Micron Shares Fall 12% in Five Sessions as Funds Add Shares | TokenPost 
 Advertisement Friday, November 20, 2026 Sections Sign in News Markets Feed Data Research Home Investing 1 min read Add as a preferred source on Google Micron Shares Fall 12% in Five Sessions as Funds Add Shares
 Micron fell 3.2% in Friday premarket trading. Third-quarter filings showed several funds increased their positions, while another cut its holding.
 By Enna Lee Published Nov 20, 2026, 7:58 AM EST Save Share A silicon memory chip sits beside a sharp cut in stone / TokenPost.ai Micron Technology (MU) fell 12% over five trading sessions through Friday’s premarket session, even as several funds increased their holdings in the chipmaker during the third quarter.
 The shares were down 3.2% in premarket trading Friday. Third-quarter filings showed Appaloosa Management lifted its position by 28% to 1.25 million shares, while Altimeter Capital added 24% to hold about 260,000 shares.
 Soros Fund Management increased its holding to nearly 36,000 shares from 22,400. Discovery Capital raised its position to nearly 15,000 shares from 1,400. The filings give no reason for the funds’ changes in holdings.
 Another fund identified as Soros Capital reduced its position by nearly 74%, to 9,400 shares from 36,700.
 Micron’s forward price-to-earnings ratio stood at 3.8, compared with 3.1 for SK Hynix and 2.5 for Samsung Electronics. Memory chipmakers often have lower valuation multiples because their business is cyclical. Micron’s forward multiple ranged from 4.5 to above 11 for much of early 2026.
 During the third quarter, Micron shares fell 7.7%, from $1,154.29 on June 30 to $1,065.11 on Sept. 30. That period is separate from the 12% decline over the five sessions through Friday’s premarket trading.
 Hewlett Packard Enterprise is scheduled to report Monday, followed by Analog Devices on Tuesday and Marvell Technology on Thursday. Their reports should shed light on AI spending trends relevant to Micron and SK Hynix.
